title: Working with Resources and Prompts
description: Implement MCP resources and prompt templates in C# servers for structured data access and reusable AI workflows.

blocks.text: Resources and prompts make your MCP server more than a function caller. Resources expose read-only data in a standardized form, and prompts let clients request pre-built prompt templates with parameters filled in.

blocks.title: Conceptual resource provider
blocks.content: Expose data through a typed resource provider.

blocks.text: Prompt templates should be deterministic and testable. Store them in code or configuration, validate arguments at invocation time, and log which template and arguments were used.

blocks.title: Version prompts carefully
blocks.text: If you change prompt wording, treat it like an API change. Document versions and test downstream clients.

items.text: My resources return structured, typed data
items.hint: Prefer JSON or typed objects over free-text responses

items.text: My prompts have validated parameters and defaults
items.hint: Validate at the server; never trust client-provided arguments blindly

items.text: I log prompt invocations for debugging
items.hint: Record template name, arguments, and timestamp

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Resources expose read-only backend data through standardized URIs.
Prompt templates enforce structure and reduce prompt drift.
Both resources and prompts should be validated and logged.
blocks.takeaway: Resources and prompts make your backend easier to use correctly and harder to misuse.
